heroText: Rome works best as a base in Italy when you anchor days around Colosseum, Roman Forum and Pantheon. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Rome Fiumicino handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with Centro Storico for the easiest first Rome stay, then compare Monti and Trastevere when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Rome hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use Centro Storico for sightseeing, Monti for a different local base, and Trastevere or Prati when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Rome unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Centro Storico for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

After the fall of the Western Roman Empire in AD 476, Rome was first under the control of Odoacer and then became part of the Ostrogothic Kingdom before returning to East Roman control after.
In 509 BC, the Romans expelled the last king from their city and established an oligarchic republic led by two annually elected consuls.
Rome then became the focus of hopes of Italian reunification after the rest of Italy was united as the Kingdom of Italy in 1861 with the temporary capital in Florence.
In 1871 the capital of Italy was moved from Florence to Rome.
